name: Loki
body:
LOKI
CR 30

XP 6,881,200
CN Medium outsider (god)
Init +24; Senses blindsight 500 ft., darkvision 60 ft., true seeing; Perception +50

DEFENSE

AC 58, touch 46, flat-footed 41 (+12 armor, +16 Dex, +1 dodge, +19 deflection)
hp 920 (40d10 +520)
Fort +25, Ref +40, Will + 31
DR 19/-; SR 41

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 +10 keen exsanguinating lightning daggers +67/+62/+57/+52 (1d4+15+1d10 electric/19-20)
Ranged +10 legendary impaling keen caustic anarcanic shortbow + 67 (1d6+1d10 acid/19-20/X3)
Special Attacks knife of the gods, sneak attack (+15d6)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 30th)

19/day–summon (any creatures, combined CR of 30 or less)

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 42, Con 34, Int 48, Wis 24, Cha 42 Base Atk +40; CMB +45; CMD +71
Feats Combat Expertise, Combat Reflexes, Deific Casting, Dodge, Greater Two-Weapon Fighting, Improved Feint, Improved Initiative, Improved Trip, Improved Two-Weapon Fighting, Legendary Magic, Mobility, Legendary Combat Reflexes*, Legendary Initiative, Quick Draw, Skill Focus (Bluff), Skill Focus (Disguise), Spring Attack, Two-Weapon Fighting, Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (dagger)
Skills Acrobatics +56, Appraise +59, Bluff +65, Climb +45, Craft (alchemy) +62, Craft (bows) +62, Craft (calligraphy) +62, Craft (traps) +62, Craft (weapons) +62, Disable Device +59, Diplomacy +59, Disguise +65, Escape Artist +56, Heal +47, Fly +56, Intimidate +56, Knowledge (planes) +62, Knowledge (religion) +62, Perception +50, Perform +56 (GM’s choice), Sense Motive +50, Sleight of Hand +56, Survival +47, Stealth +59, Swim +45

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Aligned Strike (Su)

A deity’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as being aligned to both sides of the deity’s alignment and as being epic for the purpose of resolving damage reduction.

Domain Mastery (Sp)

The deity possesses at least two domains (as per the cleric class feature) of the GM’s choice. He may use any domain powers and cast any spells associated with his domains at-will. The deity counts as a 30th level cleric for the purposes of domain powers and casting spells.

God of Mischief (Ex)

The deity is a master of trickery and misdirection. The deity may cast any spell of the illusion school as a spell-like ability. Any spell with a casting time of a standard action may be cast as a swift-action instead. At the start of each round, the deity selects one illusion he has active that may be disbelieved. Any characters that have not disbelieved this illusion are considered to be flat-footed for the purposes of dealing sneak attack damage and the deity’s knife of the gods ability. Additionally, the deity has total concealment against characters that have not disbelieved the selected illusion.

Knife of the Gods (Ex)

The deity’s affinity for stealth is unmatched by mortal beings and most immortal ones as well. When the deity wishes to harm a creature, doing so is a simple matter of making them look left while his blade comes in from the right. Each time the deity deals sneak attack damage, he may choose to either deal 90 sneak attack damage automatically (rather than rolling for sneak attack damage) or to force the target to make a DC 44 Fortitude save against L-damage (but not both).

Semi-Unlimited Wish (Sp)

The deity may cast unlimited wish once per day as a spell-like ability that does not require material components. The unlimited wish may only be in regards to something within the deity’s purview. A god of oceans could cause global draught or flooding, for instance, but could not produce any effect unrelated to oceans.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure triple standard, bracers of armor +12, two +10 keen exsanguinating lightning daggers, +10 legendary impaling keen caustic anarcanic shortbow + 67 (1d6+1d10 acid/19-20/X3)

The mischievous trickster gods are catalysts of change. Their antics trick stars into shining, mountains into moving, and gods into rearranging the rules by which the world operates. A trickster’s latest scheme might be as despicable as leading a nation to war, as noble as showing a society its own flaws and forcing them to change because of it, or as simple as hiding the sun from the sun god for a day. Whatever the intentions of Anansi, Loki, Coyote, and their ilk, one can never trust their words and always trust that things will soon become more interesting because of them.
